notes: In Mexico City many people prefer apps (Uber, DiDi) over street taxis for safety.

examples.tl: Mejor pedimos un taxi, ya es tarde.
examples.en: Let's just get a taxi, it's late already.

notes: Said 'úber'. 'Pedir un Uber' = to order an Uber. DiDi is also big in Mexico and Colombia.

examples.tl: Ya pedí el Uber, llega en cinco minutos.
examples.en: I already ordered the Uber, it arrives in five minutes.
examples.casual: Ya pedí el Uber, llega en cinco.

notes: Mexico: 'camión' = city bus (also truck). Colombia/Central America: 'bus'. Caribbean: 'guagua'. 'Autobús' is the neutral word.

examples.tl: Me voy en camión, está más barato.
examples.en: I'll take the bus, it's cheaper.

notes: Neutral word; often the long-distance coach between cities (ADO, ETN, Primera Plus in Mexico).

examples.tl: El autobús a Oaxaca sale a las diez de la noche.
examples.en: The bus to Oaxaca leaves at ten at night.

notes: Mexico City, Monterrey, Guadalajara, Medellín, Santiago, Lima all have a metro. 'Línea' = line.

examples.tl: Tomas la línea dos y te bajas en Pino Suárez.
examples.en: You take line two and get off at Pino Suárez.

notes: Mexico/Peru: 'combi' (VW van). Argentina/Peru/Colombia: 'colectivo'. Mexico City also 'pesero/micro'. You shout 'bajan' to stop.

examples.tl: La combi te deja justo en la entrada del mercado.
examples.en: The minibus drops you right at the market entrance.

notes: Cancún/Yucatán and Peru: shared van or taxi on a fixed route. In Argentina it is simply the city bus.

examples.tl: Hay colectivos a Tulum cada veinte minutos.
examples.en: There are shared vans to Tulum every twenty minutes.

notes: 'Bici' is the everyday short form of 'bicicleta'. 'Ciclovía' = bike lane.

examples.tl: Me voy en bici, hay ciclovía hasta el centro.
examples.en: I'll go by bike, there's a bike lane all the way downtown.

notes: Feminine even though it ends in -o (short for 'motocicleta'). 'Mototaxi' is common in Peru and parts of Colombia.

examples.tl: Cuidado con las motos, se meten por todos lados.
examples.en: Watch out for the motorcycles, they squeeze in everywhere.

notes: 'Carro' in Mexico, Central America, Colombia, Venezuela; 'coche' also Mexico and Spain; 'auto' in Argentina, Chile, Peru. All understood.

examples.tl: ¿Vamos en tu carro o en el mío?
examples.en: Are we taking your car or mine?

notes: Very common in central Mexico alongside 'carro'. In Argentina 'coche' is fine too but 'auto' wins.

examples.tl: Dejé el coche en el estacionamiento del centro comercial.
examples.en: I left the car in the mall parking lot.

notes: 'Manejar' is the everyday Latin American verb; 'conducir' is more formal / official (licencia de conducir).

examples.tl: Yo manejo, tú pon la dirección en el GPS.
examples.en: I'll drive, you put the address in the GPS.

examples.tl: No me gusta manejar de noche en carretera.
examples.en: I don't like driving on the highway at night.

notes: Formal register. 'Licencia de conducir' = driver's license. Irregular: yo conduzco.

examples.tl: ¿Puedo conducir aquí con mi licencia de Estados Unidos?
examples.en: Can I drive here with my US license?

notes: 'Parada de camión / de autobús'. 'Paradero' in Peru, Chile and Colombia.

examples.tl: La parada está a dos cuadras, enfrente de la farmacia.
examples.en: The stop is two blocks away, across from the pharmacy.

notes: Metro, train or bus station. Also 'estación' = season of the year.

examples.tl: Nos vemos en la estación del metro, en la salida que da al parque.
examples.en: See you at the metro station, at the exit facing the park.

notes: Mexico/Central America: 'boleto' (also for movies). 'Pasaje' = fare/ticket in much of South America. Colombia: 'tiquete'. Spain: 'billete'.

examples.tl: Compré los boletos de avión en oferta.
examples.en: I bought the plane tickets on sale.

notes: The fare you pay on a bus/combi, or a ticket in South America. 'Dar para el pasaje' = give bus money.

examples.tl: ¿Cuánto es el pasaje hasta el centro?
examples.en: How much is the fare to downtown?

accept: How much do you charge to…?
notes: Ask BEFORE getting into a street taxi with no meter. 'Cobrar' = to charge.

examples.tl: Disculpe, ¿cuánto cobra al aeropuerto?
examples.en: Excuse me, how much to the airport?

notes: 'Bajarse' = to get off/out. On a combi people shout '¡Bajan!' (someone's getting off) or '¡En la esquina, por favor!'.

examples.tl: Aquí me bajo, gracias.
examples.en: I'll get off here, thanks.

notes: Formal 'déjeme' (usted) to a driver; 'déjame' with a friend. 'Dejar' = to drop off.

examples.tl: Déjeme en la esquina, por favor, aquí está bien.
examples.en: Drop me at the corner, please, here is fine.

notes: 'Derecho' = straight ahead; 'derecha' = right. Easy to mix up. 'Recto' is also used.

examples.tl: Siga derecho hasta el semáforo y ahí da vuelta.
examples.en: Go straight to the light and turn there.

notes: 'Dar vuelta a la derecha' = turn right. 'Mano derecha' = right-hand side.

examples.tl: En la siguiente, a la derecha, por favor.
examples.en: At the next one, to the right, please.

notes: 'Voltear / dar vuelta a la izquierda' = turn left. 'Mano izquierda' = left-hand side.

examples.tl: El banco queda a la izquierda, pasando la iglesia.
examples.en: The bank is on the left, past the church.

notes: Mexico: 'dar vuelta' or 'voltear'. Colombia/Peru/Argentina: 'girar', 'doblar'. 'Dé' (usted) vs 'da' (tú). 'Dar vuelta en U' = U-turn.

examples.tl: Dé vuelta a la derecha en la gasolinera.
examples.en: Turn right at the gas station.
examples.casual: Da vuelta a la derecha en la gasolinera.

notes: Short for 'la siguiente calle'. 'En la siguiente' = at the next street/stop.

examples.tl: No, en esta no; en la siguiente.
examples.en: No, not this one; the next one.

notes: 'La pasajera' for a woman. Uber screen: 'pasajero' / 'viaje'.

examples.tl: El chofer no puede llevar más de cuatro pasajeros.
examples.en: The driver can't take more than four passengers.

notes: Latin America stresses cho-FER; Spain says CHÓ-fer. 'Conductor' is the neutral/app word.

examples.tl: El chofer del Uber me escribió que ya está afuera.
examples.en: The Uber driver texted me that he's outside already.

notes: Colombia: 'trancón'; Chile: 'taco'; Argentina: 'embotellamiento'. 'Tránsito' is also used for traffic/traffic police.

examples.tl: Perdón por la tardanza, el tráfico estaba horrible.
examples.en: Sorry I'm late, the traffic was horrible.

notes: The universal running-late text. 'Está parado' = it's at a standstill.

examples.tl: Ya voy, hay mucho tráfico en Reforma.
examples.en: On my way, there's a lot of traffic on Reforma.

notes: 'Cruzar la calle' = cross the street. 'Cruzar la frontera' = cross the border.

examples.tl: Cruza la avenida por el puente, es más seguro.
examples.en: Cross the avenue on the bridge, it's safer.

notes: Also where street vendors and windshield washers work. 'Se puso en rojo' = it turned red.

examples.tl: Pasando el semáforo, a la derecha.
examples.en: Past the traffic light, on the right.

notes: Also a pedestrian overpass ('puente peatonal') and, in Mexico, a long weekend ('hay puente el lunes').

examples.tl: Hay que cruzar por el puente peatonal, aquí no se puede.
examples.en: You have to cross on the pedestrian bridge, you can't cross here.

notes: A road between towns. 'Carretera libre' = free road vs 'autopista / de cuota' = toll road.

examples.tl: En la carretera a Puebla hubo un accidente y estuvo cerrada dos horas.
examples.en: There was an accident on the highway to Puebla and it was closed for two hours.

notes: In Mexico usually a toll road ('de cuota'). 'Periférico / Viaducto' are the Mexico City ring roads.

examples.tl: Vámonos por la autopista, aunque haya que pagar.
examples.en: Let's take the toll highway, even if we have to pay.

notes: Mexico: 'caseta (de cobro)'. Rest of Latin America: 'peaje'. 'Cuota' = the toll amount.

examples.tl: Trae efectivo, en la caseta no aceptan tarjeta.
examples.en: Bring cash, they don't take cards at the toll booth.

notes: Mexico: 'gasolinera' (people say 'la gas'). Peru: 'grifo'. Colombia: 'bomba'. 'Lleno, por favor' = fill it up.

examples.tl: Hay que cargar gasolina, nos paramos en la siguiente gasolinera.
examples.en: We need to get gas, we'll stop at the next gas station.

notes: Colombia: 'parqueadero'; Central America: 'parqueo'. 'Estacionarse' = to park. 'Vale de estacionamiento' = parking ticket stub.

examples.tl: El estacionamiento del centro comercial cobra por hora.
examples.en: The mall parking lot charges by the hour.

notes: To a taxi driver while you run in somewhere. Add 'cinco minutos' / 'un momentito'.

examples.tl: ¿Me puede esperar cinco minutos? Voy al cajero y regreso.
examples.en: Can you wait for me five minutes? I'm going to the ATM and coming back.

notes: Reflexive. 'Bajarse del camión / del carro'. Opposite: 'subirse' = to get on/in.

examples.tl: ¿En qué estación me bajo para el Zócalo?
examples.en: What station do I get off at for the Zócalo?

notes: Reflexive. 'Súbete' = get in (friend); 'súbase' = get in (usted). Also 'subir' = to go up.

examples.tl: Súbete, yo te llevo a la terminal.
examples.en: Get in, I'll take you to the terminal.

notes: 'Recoger a alguien' = pick someone up; 'pasar por ti' = swing by for you. Also pick up a package.

examples.tl: Te recojo a las ocho afuera de tu edificio.
examples.en: I'll pick you up at eight outside your building.
examples.casual: Paso por ti a las ocho.

notes: '¿Me lleva a…?' = Can you take me to…? 'Dar un aventón' (Mexico) = give a ride; Colombia 'dar la cola' is Venezuela.

examples.tl: ¿Me lleva al aeropuerto, por favor? Terminal dos.
examples.en: Can you take me to the airport, please? Terminal two.

notes: Mexico/Central America. 'Dar un aventón' = give a lift; 'pedir aventón' = hitchhike. Colombia: 'llevar'; Venezuela: 'la cola'.

examples.tl: ¿Me das un aventón al metro? Está lloviendo.
examples.en: Can you give me a ride to the metro? It's raining.

notes: 'Ponte el cinturón' = put your seat belt on. Taxi back seats often don't have working ones.

examples.tl: Ponte el cinturón, aquí sí hay multas.
examples.en: Put your seat belt on, they do give fines here.

notes: Bus routes are numbered 'Ruta 12'. Also the path your Uber takes: 'tomó otra ruta'.

examples.tl: ¿Esta ruta pasa por el hospital?
examples.en: Does this route go past the hospital?

notes: Mexico says 'placas' (plural). Chile/Argentina: 'patente'. Check the Uber plates before getting in.

examples.tl: Antes de subirte, checa que las placas coincidan con la app.
examples.en: Before getting in, check that the plates match the app.

notes: '¿Conoces un buen lugar para comer?' 'En lugar de' = instead of.

examples.tl: ¿Conoces un buen lugar para desayunar por aquí?
examples.en: Do you know a good place for breakfast around here?

notes: 'Calle cerrada' = dead end. 'En la calle' = out and about / outside.

examples.tl: Vivo en la calle Madero, número veinte.
examples.en: I live on Madero Street, number twenty.

notes: Abbreviated 'Av.' on signs and in addresses.

examples.tl: La oficina está sobre la avenida Insurgentes.
examples.en: The office is on Insurgentes Avenue.

notes: Addresses are often given as 'esquina con…' (corner of). 'En la esquina' = at the corner.

examples.tl: Es en Juárez, esquina con Reforma.
examples.en: It's on Juárez, at the corner of Reforma.

notes: Latin American word; Spain says 'manzana'. 'A dos cuadras' = two blocks away.

examples.tl: La farmacia está a tres cuadras, derecho.
examples.en: The pharmacy is three blocks away, straight ahead.

notes: An apartment building is also 'el edificio'. 'El departamento' = apartment (Mexico); 'apartamento' elsewhere.

examples.tl: Es el edificio blanco de la esquina, tercer piso.
examples.en: It's the white building on the corner, third floor.

notes: 'El centro histórico' = the old downtown. 'Centro comercial' = mall.

examples.tl: Los domingos el centro se llena de gente.
examples.en: On Sundays downtown fills up with people.

notes: In Mexico 'plaza' can also mean a shopping mall ('plaza comercial').

examples.tl: Nos vemos en la plaza, junto al quiosco.
examples.en: See you at the square, next to the bandstand.

notes: 'Tianguis' (Mexico) = open-air street market on a set day. 'Mercado sobre ruedas' too.

examples.tl: En el mercado la fruta está más barata que en el súper.
examples.en: At the market fruit is cheaper than at the supermarket.

notes: Churches are the standard landmark in directions. 'La catedral' = cathedral.

examples.tl: Pasando la iglesia, la primera a la izquierda.
examples.en: Past the church, the first on the left.

notes: 'La hora de la salida de la escuela' = school pickup, a traffic nightmare. 'El colegio' = private school.

examples.tl: A las dos hay mucho tráfico por la escuela.
examples.en: At two there's a lot of traffic because of the school.

notes: 'Clínica' is also common. 'Urgencias' = emergency room.

examples.tl: ¿Dónde queda el hospital más cercano?
examples.en: Where is the nearest hospital?

notes: Mexico: 'el Parque México', 'Chapultepec'. Colombians say 'parque' for a neighborhood square too.

examples.tl: Déjeme en la entrada del parque, por favor.
examples.en: Drop me at the park entrance, please.

notes: 'Ir a la playa' = go to the beach. 'Playero' = beachwear/beach-related.

examples.tl: El fin de semana nos vamos a la playa.
examples.en: This weekend we're going to the beach.

notes: 'El cerro' = hill / smaller mountain, very common in Latin America. 'La sierra' = mountain range.

examples.tl: Desde el pueblo se ven las montañas con nieve.
examples.en: From the town you can see the snowy mountains.

notes: Also 'the people' (el pueblo mexicano). Mexico's 'Pueblos Mágicos' are tourist towns.

examples.tl: Mi familia es de un pueblo cerca de Guanajuato.
examples.en: My family is from a town near Guanajuato.

notes: 'La Ciudad de México' (CDMX). Locals also say 'el DF' (old name).

examples.tl: La ciudad es enorme, se tarda una hora en cruzarla.
examples.en: The city is huge, it takes an hour to cross it.

notes: Taxis from the airport are usually prepaid at a booth ('taxi autorizado').

examples.tl: Llego al aeropuerto a las seis, ¿me recoges?
examples.en: I get to the airport at six, will you pick me up?

notes: Veracruz, Puerto Vallarta, Cartagena. 'El muelle' = pier/dock.

examples.tl: El ferry sale del puerto a las ocho.
examples.en: The ferry leaves from the port at eight.

notes: Mexico City: 'la TAPO', 'Central del Norte'. Feminine for the bus station; 'la terminal dos' at the airport too.

examples.tl: ¿A qué hora tienes que estar en la terminal?
examples.en: What time do you have to be at the terminal?

notes: Colombia says 'droguería'. Many have a cheap doctor's office next door ('consultorio').

examples.tl: Hay una farmacia 24 horas en la esquina.
examples.en: There's a 24-hour pharmacy on the corner.

notes: Also 'bench'. 'El cajero (automático)' = ATM.

examples.tl: ¿Hay un cajero del banco cerca de aquí?
examples.en: Is there one of the bank's ATMs near here?

notes: 'Río' needs the accent. Many Mexico City avenues are named after old rivers (Río Churubusco).

examples.tl: El pueblo está del otro lado del río.
examples.en: The town is on the other side of the river.

notes: Mexico: 'colonia' (Col. Roma, Col. Condesa). Everywhere else: 'barrio'. Also 'cologne' (perfume).

examples.tl: ¿En qué colonia vives? ¿Está lejos del metro?
examples.en: What neighborhood do you live in? Is it far from the metro?

notes: Neutral Latin American word. In Mexico 'barrio' can imply a rougher area; 'colonia' is the formal unit.

examples.tl: Es un barrio tranquilo, puedes caminar de noche.
examples.en: It's a quiet neighborhood, you can walk at night.

notes: Mexican word for the main plaza of a city or town. Elsewhere: 'la plaza mayor / plaza principal / parque central'.

examples.tl: Hay concierto gratis en el Zócalo el sábado.
examples.en: There's a free concert at the Zócalo on Saturday.

notes: Seaside promenade: Puerto Vallarta, Havana, Lima's Miraflores. Where everyone walks at sunset.

examples.tl: Vamos a caminar por el malecón al atardecer.
examples.en: Let's walk along the boardwalk at sunset.

notes: Masculine despite -a. 'Mándame tu ubicación' = send me your location (WhatsApp pin).

examples.tl: Mándame la ubicación por WhatsApp y lo busco en el mapa.
examples.en: Send me the location on WhatsApp and I'll find it on the map.

notes: What you share on WhatsApp. '¿Dónde te ubicas?' = where are you (located)?

examples.tl: Pásame tu ubicación y pido el Uber hasta ahí.
examples.en: Send me your location and I'll order the Uber to there.

notes: Both 'address' and 'direction'. Mexican addresses: calle, número, colonia, código postal.

examples.tl: ¿Cuál es la dirección exacta? Para ponerla en la app.
examples.en: What's the exact address? So I can put it in the app.

notes: '¿Adónde vas?' = where are you going (to)? '¿De dónde eres?' = where are you from?

examples.tl: ¿Dónde está la salida del metro?
examples.en: Where is the metro exit?

notes: 'Quedar' for the location of places is very Latin American and sounds natural. 'Queda lejos' = it's far.

examples.tl: Disculpe, ¿dónde queda la oficina de migración?
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the immigration office?

notes: 'Cerca de' = near (something). 'Cerquita' = really close (diminutive, everywhere in Latin America).

examples.tl: Está cerca, a cinco minutos caminando.
examples.en: It's close, a five-minute walk.

notes: 'Lejos de' = far from. '¿Está lejos?' is the first thing you ask before walking.

examples.tl: No, en Uber está lejos; mejor vete en metro.
examples.en: No, by Uber it's far; better take the metro.

notes: 'Acá' is also common (very common in Argentina/Colombia). 'Por aquí' = around here / this way.

examples.tl: Aquí está bien, gracias.
examples.en: Here is fine, thanks.

notes: 'Ahí' = there (near); 'allá' = over there (farther). People point and say 'allá'.

examples.tl: ¿Ve esa torre? Allá es.
examples.en: See that tower? It's over there.

notes: 'Al lado' alone = next door. 'Del otro lado' = on the other side.

examples.tl: El Oxxo está al lado de la gasolinera.
examples.en: The Oxxo is next to the gas station.

notes: 'Enfrente' = facing / across the street. 'Frente a' is the same.

examples.tl: Espérame enfrente del banco, en la banqueta.
examples.en: Wait for me across from the bank, on the sidewalk.

notes: 'Atrás de' is the colloquial Latin American form you'll hear more often. 'Por atrás' = around the back.

examples.tl: La entrada al estacionamiento está detrás del edificio.
examples.en: The parking entrance is behind the building.
examples.casual: La entrada está atrás del edificio.

notes: 'Adelante' = ahead / go ahead. 'Más adelante' = farther along (very common in directions).

examples.tl: Más adelante hay un puente; la casa está justo delante del puente.
examples.en: Farther along there's a bridge; the house is right in front of the bridge.

notes: Slightly more formal than 'al lado de'. 'Juntos' = together.

examples.tl: Hay un cajero junto a la entrada del metro.
examples.en: There's an ATM right next to the metro entrance.

notes: Addresses: 'entre Madero y 5 de Mayo' = between Madero and 5 de Mayo streets.

examples.tl: Es en Durango, entre Oaxaca y Tonalá.
examples.en: It's on Durango, between Oaxaca and Tonalá.

notes: 'Adentro' is the spoken Latin American form; 'dentro de' before a noun. 'Pásale' (Mexico) = come in.

examples.tl: Te espero adentro, hace mucho calor afuera.
examples.en: I'll wait for you inside, it's really hot outside.

notes: 'Ya estoy afuera' = the Uber driver's text. 'Fuera de' before a noun.

examples.tl: Ya estoy afuera, en el carro gris.
examples.en: I'm outside already, in the gray car.

notes: 'Allá arriba' = up there. 'Para arriba' = uphill / up this way.

examples.tl: El baño está arriba, al fondo.
examples.en: The bathroom is upstairs, at the end.

notes: 'Para abajo' = downhill. 'Aquí abajo' = down here. Also what you yell in a combi: '¡Bajan!'.

examples.tl: Te espero abajo, en la entrada del edificio.
examples.en: I'll wait for you downstairs, at the building entrance.

notes: 'Al final de la calle' = at the end of the street. 'Al fondo' = at the back/end (inside a building).

examples.tl: Sigue hasta el final de la calle y ahí está.
examples.en: Keep going to the end of the street and it's right there.

notes: Also an admission ticket ('la entrada al museo cuesta 90 pesos'). 'Entrada principal' = main entrance.

examples.tl: Nos vemos en la entrada principal del mercado.
examples.en: See you at the main entrance of the market.

notes: Also departure (flights: 'salidas / llegadas'). Metro exits are numbered or named by street.

examples.tl: Toma la salida que dice Avenida Juárez.
examples.en: Take the exit that says Juárez Avenue.

notes: Gerund of 'pasar' used in directions: 'pasando el puente' = once you pass the bridge.

examples.tl: Está pasando el semáforo, a mano derecha.
examples.en: It's just past the traffic light, on the right-hand side.

notes: 'Llegar a' = arrive at. 'Ya llegué' = I'm here (the text when you arrive). 'Llegar tarde' = be late.

examples.tl: Ya llegué, estoy en la puerta.
examples.en: I'm here, I'm at the door.

examples.tl: ¿A qué hora llega tu vuelo?
examples.en: What time does your flight get in?

notes: Two uses: go past a place ('pasas por la iglesia') and swing by for someone ('paso por ti').

examples.tl: Paso por ti a las siete, ¿va?
examples.en: I'll swing by for you at seven, okay?

notes: No 'para' after it: 'busco la estación'. In Colombia/Caribbean 'buscar a alguien' also = pick someone up.

examples.tl: Estoy buscando la calle Regina, ¿sabe dónde queda?
examples.en: I'm looking for Regina Street, do you know where it is?

notes: Reflexive. 'Me perdí' = I got lost. Also 'to miss' (an event): 'te lo perdiste'.

examples.tl: Me perdí saliendo del metro, todas las calles se parecen.
examples.en: I got lost coming out of the metro, all the streets look alike.

notes: 'Perdida' if the speaker is a woman. Follow with '¿me puede ayudar?'.

examples.tl: Disculpe, estoy perdido. ¿Para el Zócalo?
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm lost. Which way to the Zócalo?

notes: Mexico/Central America prefer 'regresar'; 'volver' everywhere. Colombia: 'devolverse' = turn back. 'De regreso' = on the way back.

examples.tl: Regreso a Estados Unidos en diciembre.
examples.en: I'm going back to the US in December.

examples.tl: Te pasaste; hay que regresar una cuadra.
examples.en: You went too far; we have to go back a block.

notes: The basic directions question. Answer often starts 'Te vas derecho…' or 'Agarra…'.

examples.tl: Disculpe, ¿cómo llego a la terminal de autobuses?
examples.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the bus terminal?

notes: '¿Qué tan…?' = 'how (adjective)' in Latin America. '¿Se puede ir caminando?' = can you walk it?

examples.tl: ¿Qué tan lejos está? ¿Se puede ir caminando?
examples.en: How far is it? Can you walk there?

notes: Polite opener to a guard or shopkeeper. 'Indicar' = point out. 'Joven' or 'señor/señora' to get attention.

examples.tl: Joven, ¿me puede indicar dónde está la salida?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you show me where the exit is?

notes: Mexico: 'agarra la primera a la derecha', 'agarrar un taxi'. Avoid 'coger' in Mexico/Argentina (vulgar); fine in Colombia/Spain.

examples.tl: Agarra Insurgentes y te vas derecho hasta Reforma.
examples.en: Take Insurgentes and go straight until Reforma.

notes: Mexico: 'banqueta'. Colombia: 'andén'. Peru/Argentina: 'vereda'. 'Acera' is the neutral word.

examples.tl: Espérame en la banqueta de enfrente.
examples.en: Wait for me on the sidewalk across the street.

notes: 'Caminando' = on foot: 'está a diez minutos caminando'. 'A pie' also.

examples.tl: Mejor vamos caminando, está a dos cuadras.
examples.en: Let's just walk, it's two blocks away.

notes: '¡Buen viaje!' = have a good trip. 'Viaje de trabajo' = business trip. Uber calls each ride 'un viaje'.

examples.tl: ¿Cómo estuvo el viaje? ¿Llegaste bien?
examples.en: How was the trip? Did you get in okay?

notes: 'Viajar en avión / en autobús / por tierra'. Regular -ar verb.

examples.tl: Me gusta viajar en autobús, se ve el paisaje.
examples.en: I like traveling by bus, you get to see the scenery.

notes: Always plural in Spanish. 'Estar de vacaciones' = be on vacation. 'Semana Santa' is the big travel week.

examples.tl: En Semana Santa todo el mundo sale de vacaciones y las carreteras se llenan.
examples.en: During Holy Week everyone goes on vacation and the highways fill up.

notes: At immigration: '¿Motivo del viaje?' — 'Vengo de vacaciones / turismo'.

examples.tl: Vengo de vacaciones, dos semanas.
examples.en: I'm here on vacation, two weeks.

notes: Irregular: yo salgo. 'Salir de viaje' = go away on a trip. 'Ya salí' = I just left (texting).

examples.tl: Ya salí, llego en veinte minutos.
examples.en: I just left, I'll be there in twenty minutes.

examples.tl: El camión sale a las nueve en punto.
examples.en: The bus leaves at nine sharp.

notes: Polite way to say you're busy / can't make it. 'Compromiso' is not 'compromise'.

examples.tl: Mañana no puedo, tengo un compromiso en la tarde.
examples.en: I can't tomorrow, I have something I committed to in the afternoon.

notes: 'Vuelo directo' = nonstop; 'con escala' = with a layover. 'Volar' = to fly.

examples.tl: Mi vuelo sale a las seis de la mañana, tengo que estar a las cuatro.
examples.en: My flight leaves at six in the morning, I have to be there at four.

notes: 'Hacer escala en Panamá' = have a layover in Panama. 'Vuelo directo' = nonstop.

examples.tl: Tengo una escala de tres horas en Ciudad de México.
examples.en: I have a three-hour layover in Mexico City.

notes: 'El vuelo está retrasado / viene con retraso'. 'Demorado' in Colombia/Peru. Careful: 'retrasado' about a person is an insult.

examples.tl: El vuelo está retrasado una hora por el clima.
examples.en: The flight is delayed an hour because of the weather.

notes: Mexico: 'documentar (el equipaje)' = check in / check bags. Elsewhere 'hacer el check-in'. 'Pase de abordar' = boarding pass.

examples.tl: Ya documenté en línea, solo voy a dejar la maleta.
examples.en: I already checked in online, I'm just going to drop off the suitcase.

notes: Mexico: 'pase de abordar'. South America/Spain: 'tarjeta de embarque'. 'Abordar' = to board; 'puerta' = gate.

examples.tl: Tenga su pase de abordar y su pasaporte a la mano.
examples.en: Have your boarding pass and passport ready.

notes: Singular, uncountable. 'Equipaje de mano' = carry-on. 'Reclamo de equipaje' = baggage claim.

examples.tl: Solo llevo equipaje de mano, no documento nada.
examples.en: I'm only taking a carry-on, I'm not checking anything.

notes: Argentina: 'valija'. 'Hacer la maleta' = pack. 'Se me perdió la maleta' = my bag got lost.

examples.tl: Mi maleta pesa veinticinco kilos, creo que me van a cobrar.
examples.en: My suitcase weighs twenty-five kilos, I think they're going to charge me.

notes: 'Mochilero' = backpacker. In crowded metros wear it in front ('la mochila adelante').

examples.tl: En el metro lleva la mochila adelante.
examples.en: On the metro wear your backpack in front.

notes: Silent h: 'o-TEL'. 'Hostal' = hostel. 'Airbnb' said 'air-bi-en-bi'.

examples.tl: El hotel está a diez minutos del aeropuerto.
examples.en: The hotel is ten minutes from the airport.

notes: 'Tengo una reservación a nombre de…' (Mexico) / 'una reserva' (South America, Spain).

examples.tl: Ya reservé el hotel, dos noches con desayuno.
examples.en: I already booked the hotel, two nights with breakfast.

notes: Mexico/Central America: 'reservación'. South America and Spain: 'reserva'.

examples.tl: Buenas noches, tengo una reservación a nombre de Johnson.
examples.en: Good evening, I have a reservation under Johnson.

notes: Formal hotel word. 'Cuarto' is the everyday word in Mexico. 'Sencilla / doble' = single / double.

examples.tl: ¿Tiene una habitación doble para esta noche?
examples.en: Do you have a double room for tonight?

notes: Cozumel, Isla Mujeres, Holbox. 'El ferry' or 'la lancha' (small boat) to get there.

examples.tl: A la isla se llega en ferry desde Playa del Carmen.
examples.en: You get to the island by ferry from Playa del Carmen.

notes: English word, fully adopted. 'Excursión' is also common; 'recorrido' = a guided walk/route.

examples.tl: Contratamos un tour a las pirámides con todo incluido.
examples.en: We booked an all-inclusive tour to the pyramids.

notes: Also 'memory'. 'Artesanías' = handicrafts, what you actually buy at the market. 'Souvenir' also used.

examples.tl: Compré unos recuerdos para mi mamá en el mercado de artesanías.
examples.en: I bought some souvenirs for my mom at the crafts market.

notes: Preterite of 'llegar'. 'Se me hizo tarde' = I ran late (it got late on me) is the usual excuse.

examples.tl: Llegué tarde a la cita por el tráfico.
examples.en: I got to the appointment late because of the traffic.

notes: 'Tempranito' = nice and early. 'Más temprano' = earlier.

examples.tl: Hay que salir temprano para no agarrar tráfico.
examples.en: We have to leave early so we don't hit traffic.

notes: Adverb 'tarde' = late; noun 'la tarde' = afternoon. 'Se me hizo tarde' = I ran late.

examples.tl: Ya es tarde, mejor pide un Uber.
examples.en: It's late already, better order an Uber.

notes: Carry a copy; the original stays in the hotel safe. 'Vigente' = valid; 'vencido' = expired.

examples.tl: ¿Trajiste tu pasaporte? Lo piden en migración.
examples.en: Did you bring your passport? They ask for it at immigration.

notes: Same form for la turista. 'Zona turística' = tourist area. 'Gringo' is the casual word for Americans, not always rude.

examples.tl: En diciembre Cancún se llena de turistas.
examples.en: In December Cancún fills up with tourists.

notes: 'Pasar por la aduana' = go through customs. 'Declarar' = declare. In Mexico you may press a button for a random check.

examples.tl: En la aduana me revisaron la maleta completa.
examples.en: At customs they searched my whole suitcase.

notes: Mexico: 'migración' or 'el INM'. 'La migra' = US immigration enforcement (colloquial). 'Residencia temporal' = temporary residency.

examples.tl: Mañana tengo cita en migración para renovar mi residencia.
examples.en: Tomorrow I have an appointment at immigration to renew my residency.

en: How many days are you staying?
notes: The immigration officer's question (usted). Answer: 'Dos semanas' / 'Seis meses'. 'Quedarse' = to stay.

examples.tl: —¿Cuántos días se queda? —Tres semanas, de vacaciones.
examples.en: —How many days are you staying? —Three weeks, on vacation.

notes: Reflexive. '¿Dónde te quedas?' = where are you staying? 'Me quedo en un Airbnb'.

examples.tl: ¿Dónde te vas a quedar en Medellín?
examples.en: Where are you going to stay in Medellín?

notes: Latin American verb; Spain says 'hacer la maleta'. 'Desempacar' = unpack.

examples.tl: Todavía no he empacado y el vuelo es mañana.
examples.en: I still haven't packed and the flight is tomorrow.

notes: 'Vámonos' = let's leave (from here); 'vamos' = let's go (to somewhere). Mexico adds '¡Ándale!' / '¡Órale!'.

examples.tl: Ya llegó el Uber, ¡vámonos!
examples.en: The Uber's here, let's go!

notes: Mexican 'tardado' = slow, time-consuming. Elsewhere '¡Qué demora!' or '¡Cómo se demora!'.

examples.tl: ¡Qué tardado! Llevamos media hora en la fila de migración.
examples.en: This is taking forever! We've been in the immigration line half an hour.

notes: Also 'to hope/expect'. 'Espérame' = wait for me. 'Espéreme' with usted.

examples.tl: Espérame en la entrada, ya casi llego.
examples.en: Wait for me at the entrance, I'm almost there.

notes: Said at the terminal, in WhatsApp, by the hotel desk. Reply: 'Gracias, nos vemos'.

examples.tl: ¡Buen viaje! Avísame cuando llegues.
examples.en: Have a good trip! Let me know when you arrive.

en: Let me know when you arrive
accept: Text me when you get there
notes: 'Avisar' = let know / notify. Standard send-off text; reply 'Ya llegué'.

examples.tl: Cuídate y avísame cuando llegues a casa.
examples.en: Take care and let me know when you get home.

notes: 'Cruzar la frontera' = cross the border. 'La garita' = border checkpoint (Tijuana).

examples.tl: En la frontera la fila para cruzar duró dos horas.
examples.en: At the border the line to cross took two hours.

notes: Mexico: 'hacer fila'. Elsewhere 'hacer cola'. '¿Es la fila para…?' = is this the line for…?

examples.tl: ¿Esta es la fila para documentar?
examples.en: Is this the line for check-in?

notes: Taxis: not expected. Restaurants: 10-15%. Gas station attendants and baggers: a few pesos.

examples.tl: Déjale propina al que te ayudó con las maletas.
examples.en: Leave a tip for the guy who helped you with the bags.

notes: 'Temporada de lluvias' = rainy season (Mexico: June–October, every afternoon).

examples.tl: Con la lluvia el tráfico se pone peor.
examples.en: With the rain the traffic gets worse.

notes: 'Llueve' = it rains / it's raining; spoken Spanish prefers 'está lloviendo'. 'Un aguacero' = downpour. Mexico: 'está cayendo un chubasco'.

examples.tl: Está lloviendo muy fuerte, espérate a que pase.
examples.en: It's raining really hard, wait for it to pass.

notes: 'Se inundó la calle' = the street flooded. 'Encharcamiento' = big puddles (Mexico City traffic reports).

examples.tl: Hubo inundación en el Periférico y cerraron dos carriles.
examples.en: There was flooding on the Periférico and they closed two lanes.

notes: Masculine in standard Spanish ('la calor' is rural/colloquial). 'Tengo calor' = I'm hot (never 'estoy caliente').

examples.tl: Con este calor no se puede caminar al mediodía.
examples.en: In this heat you can't walk around at noon.

notes: Weather uses 'hacer': hace calor / frío / viento / sol. 'Hace un calorón' = it's scorching (Mexico).

examples.tl: Hace mucho calor, ¿el carro tiene aire?
examples.en: It's really hot, does the car have AC?

notes: 'Hace frío' = it's cold out; 'tengo frío' = I'm cold. Mountain towns get cold at night even in summer.

examples.tl: En la noche hace frío en la montaña, llévate un suéter.
examples.en: At night it gets cold in the mountains, take a sweater.

notes: 'Tormenta eléctrica' = thunderstorm. 'Tormenta tropical' is one step below a hurricane.

examples.tl: Cancelaron el vuelo por la tormenta.
examples.en: They canceled the flight because of the storm.

notes: Season June–November on both coasts. 'Categoría tres'. 'Alerta roja' = red alert.

examples.tl: Viene un huracán, cerraron el aeropuerto de Cancún.
examples.en: A hurricane is coming, they closed the Cancún airport.

notes: The announcement when weather or a strike shuts schools. 'Suspendieron clases' is the official version.

examples.tl: Por la tormenta no hay clases mañana en todo el estado.
examples.en: Because of the storm there's no school tomorrow in the whole state.

notes: Same form singular and plural. Mexico and Central America often say 'sombrilla' for a rain umbrella too.

examples.tl: Llévate el paraguas, en la tarde siempre llueve.
examples.en: Take the umbrella, it always rains in the afternoon.

notes: 'Me mojé' = I got wet. 'Empapado' = soaked through. 'Mojarse' = get wet.

examples.tl: Llegué todo mojado, me agarró la lluvia saliendo del metro.
examples.en: I got here soaking wet, the rain caught me coming out of the metro.

notes: Latin America says 'el clima' for today's weather; Spain says 'el tiempo'. '¿Cómo está el clima allá?'

examples.tl: ¿Cómo está el clima en Monterrey? ¿Llevo chamarra?
examples.en: How's the weather in Monterrey? Should I bring a jacket?

notes: 'Hace sol' = it's sunny. 'Bloqueador' = sunscreen. 'Me quemé' = I got sunburned.

examples.tl: Hay mucho sol, ponte bloqueador y gorra.
examples.en: It's very sunny, put on sunscreen and a cap.

notes: '¡Aguas!' is the very Mexican shout for 'watch out!'. '¡Ojo!' = heads up. 'Cuidado con…' = careful with…

examples.tl: ¡Cuidado! Viene una moto.
examples.en: Careful! There's a motorcycle coming.

notes: Standard goodbye. 'Cuídese' for usted. Reply: 'Igualmente' or 'Tú también'.

examples.tl: Bueno, ya me voy. Cuídate, nos vemos el lunes.
examples.en: Okay, I'm off. Take care, see you Monday.

notes: 'Ten' is the tú imperative of tener; 'tenga' for usted. 'Ten cuidado con tu celular' = watch your phone.

examples.tl: Ten cuidado con tu celular en el metro, hay mucho ratero.
examples.en: Be careful with your phone on the metro, there are a lot of pickpockets.

notes: 'Peligrosa' for feminine nouns. 'El peligro' = danger. 'Es zona peligrosa' is what locals say about a neighborhood.

examples.tl: Esa zona es peligrosa de noche, no vayas solo.
examples.en: That area is dangerous at night, don't go alone.

notes: Three meanings: safe ('es seguro'), sure ('¿estás seguro?'), and the noun 'el seguro' = insurance / lock.

examples.tl: ¿Es seguro caminar por aquí de noche?
examples.en: Is it safe to walk around here at night?

examples.tl: ¿Tu seguro de viaje cubre hospital?
examples.en: Does your travel insurance cover hospital?

notes: 'Me asaltaron' = I got mugged. 'Robo' = theft in general; 'atraco' in Colombia.

examples.tl: Hubo un asalto en esa parada la semana pasada.
examples.en: There was a mugging at that bus stop last week.

notes: 'Me asaltaron' / 'me robaron' = I got mugged / robbed. 'Me robaron el celular' = they stole my phone.

examples.tl: A mi primo lo asaltaron saliendo del cajero.
examples.en: My cousin got mugged leaving the ATM.

notes: 'La policía' = the force; 'el/la policía' = an officer (Mexico also 'el poli'). Emergency number: 911 in Mexico, 123 in Colombia.

examples.tl: Si pasa algo, marca al 911 o busca a la policía.
examples.en: If something happens, call 911 or find the police.

notes: Every building, mall and parking lot has one; they are the best people to ask for directions. Peru/Central America: 'guachimán'.

examples.tl: Pregúntale al vigilante, él sabe en qué piso es.
examples.en: Ask the security guard, he knows which floor it is.

notes: Said by a guard or local steering you away. 'Por aquí' = this way; 'por allá' = that way.

examples.tl: Por aquí no, está cerrado. Dé la vuelta por la otra calle.
examples.en: Not this way, it's closed. Go around on the other street.

notes: On signs: 'Prohibido estacionarse', 'Prohibido el paso' = no entry. 'No se permite' = not allowed.

examples.tl: Dice 'prohibido el paso', mejor vamos por el otro lado.
examples.en: It says 'no entry', let's go the other way.

notes: Mexican colloquial word for a petty thief. 'Ladrón' is neutral everywhere. 'Carterista' = pickpocket (formal).

examples.tl: En el metro hay mucho ratero, guarda la cartera adelante.
examples.en: There are a lot of pickpockets on the metro, keep your wallet in front.

notes: Neutral word across Latin America. '¡Ladrón!' is the shout. Feminine: 'la ladrona'.

examples.tl: Un ladrón le arrebató el celular en el semáforo.
examples.en: A thief snatched her phone at the traffic light.

notes: 'Está oscuro' = it's dark. 'Ya está oscureciendo' = it's getting dark. Streets without lights: 'no hay alumbrado'.

examples.tl: Esa calle está muy oscura, mejor nos vamos por la avenida.
examples.en: That street is really dark, let's go along the avenue instead.

notes: 'Choque' = car crash (Mexico: 'chocar' = to crash). 'Hubo un accidente' is why the highway is closed.

examples.tl: Hubo un accidente en la carretera y está parado el tráfico.
examples.en: There was an accident on the highway and traffic is at a standstill.

notes: 'Ir solo' = go alone; 'sola' for a woman. Also the adverb 'only' ('solo quiero…').

examples.tl: No vayas solo a esa zona, mejor ve con alguien.
examples.en: Don't go to that area alone, better go with someone.

notes: 'Dar miedo' = to be scary (lit. 'give fear'). 'Me da miedo' = it scares me. 'Tengo miedo' = I'm scared.

examples.tl: Esa calle de noche da miedo, no hay ni una luz.
examples.en: That street at night is scary, there's not a single light.

notes: Reason to leave or take an Uber instead of walking. 'Ya es muy tarde' = it's too late (also for missed chances).

examples.tl: Ya es tarde, mejor pide un Uber, no te vayas caminando.
examples.en: It's late already, better order an Uber, don't walk.

notes: Latin America: 'celular' / 'cel'. Spain: 'móvil'. 'No saques el celular en la calle' is standard advice.

examples.tl: No saques el celular en la calle, guárdalo.
examples.en: Don't take your phone out on the street, put it away.

notes: Mexico: wallet. Argentina/Colombia: 'cartera' = woman's purse, 'billetera' = wallet. 'La bolsa' = handbag (Mexico).

examples.tl: Lleva solo lo necesario en la cartera, nada de pasaporte.
examples.en: Carry only what you need in your wallet, no passport.

notes: '¡Auxilio!' is the common emergency shout in Mexico. 'Ayudar' = to help; '¿Me puede ayudar?' = can you help me?

examples.tl: ¿Me puede ayudar? Me robaron la mochila.
examples.en: Can you help me? They stole my backpack.

notes: 'Es una emergencia' gets a taxi to hurry. Mexico 911, Colombia 123, Peru 105, Argentina 911. 'Urgencias' = ER.

examples.tl: Es una emergencia, lléveme al hospital más cercano.
examples.en: It's an emergency, take me to the nearest hospital.

notes: 'Es una zona tranquila' = safe neighborhood. As an interjection 'Tranquilo' = relax, no worries. 'Tranqui' in texting.

examples.tl: Es un barrio tranquilo, hay vigilancia toda la noche.
examples.en: It's a quiet neighborhood, there's security all night.

notes: To squeeze past someone on a bus or in a market. Reply: 'Propio' or 'Pase'. 'Disculpe' is for getting attention.

examples.tl: Con permiso, bajo en esta.
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm getting off at this one.

notes: Usted form to start a question with a stranger. 'Disculpa' (tú) for younger people. 'Oiga' = hey (usted), more direct.

examples.tl: Disculpe, ¿este camión va al centro?
examples.en: Excuse me, does this bus go downtown?

notes: Also 'cashier'. Use ATMs inside banks or malls, not on the street at night. 'Retirar' = withdraw.

examples.tl: Busca un cajero dentro del centro comercial, es más seguro.
examples.en: Find an ATM inside the mall, it's safer.

notes: 'En efectivo' = in cash. Combis, markets and toll booths are cash only. 'Cambio' / 'feria' (Mexico) = small change.

examples.tl: ¿Aceptan tarjeta o solo efectivo?
examples.en: Do you take cards or only cash?

notes: Mexico City: 'Hoy No Circula' bans cars by plate number on certain days; fines apply. 'Mordida' = bribe (colloquial).

examples.tl: Me pusieron una multa por estacionarme en la banqueta.
examples.en: They gave me a fine for parking on the sidewalk.

notes: Mexico: 'licencia de conducir / de manejo'. Colombia: 'pase'. A US license is valid for tourists in Mexico.

examples.tl: El policía me pidió la licencia y la tarjeta de circulación.
examples.en: The officer asked me for my license and the registration.

notes: Mexico/Central America/Colombia: 'llanta'. Argentina/Caribbean: 'goma'. 'Se me ponchó una llanta' (Mexico) = I got a flat.

examples.tl: Se nos ponchó una llanta en la carretera, llegamos tarde.
examples.en: We got a flat tire on the highway, we got there late.

notes: Uber's 'tarifa dinámica' = surge pricing. 'Tarifa fija' = fixed fare (airport taxis).

examples.tl: Hay tarifa dinámica por la lluvia, el Uber está carísimo.
examples.en: There's surge pricing because of the rain, the Uber is super expensive.

notes: '¿Cuál es el horario del metro?' 'Horario de verano' = daylight saving time (Mexico mostly dropped it in 2022).

examples.tl: ¿Cuál es el horario del último metro? No quiero quedarme sin cómo regresar.
examples.en: What time is the last metro? I don't want to be left with no way back.
